body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\theta_{\kappa_T(C)}=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_1,M_1]}\{(T-\kappa_T(C))^{-1}\sum_{t=\kappa_T(C)+1}^{T}Y_t\prod_{j=t-\kappa_T(C)}^{t}e(A_j\mid X_j)/b(A_j\mid X_j)\}\), and, uniformly over \(C\ge1\), \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\asymp T^{-1}+T^{-2/(2+t_0\zeta)}q_C^{2t_0\zeta/(2+t_0\zeta)}\), with comparison constants depending only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\).

sampling_model.design: One behavior-stationary trajectory from a time-homogeneous finite POMDP; the supplied design tag contains the finite observed and action alphabets and the known behavior and target policies, while the hidden alphabet and kernel are not supplied.
sampling_model.units: The observations are \((X_t,A_t,Y_t)\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\); \(H_t\) and both stationary joint-state laws are unobserved.
sampling_model.treatment: The action alphabet is any nonempty finite set of unrestricted cardinality in the upper model class; the matching lower bound uses a binary-action bounded subclass.
sampling_model.overlap: One-step action ratios are bounded by \(e^{\zeta}\), and the unobserved joint stationary ratio is bounded by \(C\). The normalized radius used by the theorem is \(q_C=(C-1)/C\); neither stationary law nor its ratio is supplied.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No latent alphabet, transition kernel, reward regression, stationary law, proxy, emission rank, or finite-memory bound is known or imposed on the estimator. The attaining tagged rule uses only the observed trajectory, supplied design, and fixed structural constants.
sampling_model.outcomes: Rewards are real and satisfy Hu and Wager's pointwise conditional mean and second-moment envelope with fixed \(0<M_1<\sqrt{M_2}\); bounded support is used only by the lower-bound subclass and the finite illustration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives a single-trajectory minimax lower bound of order \(T^{-2/(t_0\zeta+2)}\) under mixing, action overlap, and conditional reward moments, while Section 3.2 leaves distributionally overlapping hidden-state hard instances open.

Strong or square-integrable stationary density-ratio control supports root-\(T\) behavior for truncated doubly robust evaluation in fully observed MDPs, while heavier ratio tails produce slower regimes.
Latent-state density-ratio coverage is weaker than belief coverage, and future-dependent value guarantees can retain exponentially large outcome or belief quantities without stronger conditions.
Generic partially observable off-policy evaluation can have arbitrarily large bias, while recovery in the decoupled POMDP uses invertibility and conditional-independence structure.
Double reinforcement learning attains the semiparametric efficiency bound in observed Markov models using estimated \(q\)-functions and marginalized density ratios.
Long-run average policy outcomes admit estimation and confidence intervals in a fully observed Markov mobile-health model.

body.tldr: For Hu and Wager's single-trajectory conditional-moment POMDP class, strengthened by latent stationary overlap \(d_e\le Cd_b\), the exact cardinality-uniform minimax risk is \(R_T(t_0,\zeta,C)\asymp T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\), uniformly for every \(C\ge1\), where \(q_C=(C-1)/C\) and \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\). The comparison constants depend on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\) but not on \(C\), \(T\), or alphabet cardinalities. Radius-adaptive observable PHIW attains the law, and a moment-scaled signed-depth pair gives the matching all-estimator converse. The exact elbow is \(q_C\asymp T^{-1/2}\), equivalently \(C_T-1\asymp T^{-1/2}\) near equality: equality is parametric, while every fixed \(C>1\) retains the Hu--Wager hidden-state exponent, with no logarithmic loss.

project_justification.gap: HuWager2023 establishes the unrestricted conditional-moment minimax exponent but leaves overlapping hidden-state hard instances open and supplies no phase diagram indexed by a latent stationary-overlap radius.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a uniform-in-\(C\) observed-law modulus that joins exact stationary-law equality, shrinking overlap, and fixed overlap without observing the latent density ratio.
project_justification.fill: A radius-sensitive PHIW covariance proof and a moment-scaled signed-depth family establish the full frontier \(T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\), including a \(C\)-independent observed-path KL constant and a tagged-design minimax formulation.

body.related_work: HuWager2023 is the theorem anchor: its Model 3 and Theorem 2.1 work with arbitrary finite actions and pointwise conditional first- and second-moment reward envelopes, while Theorem 3.1 gives the unrestricted single-trajectory exponent and Section 3.2 leaves a distributionally overlapping hidden-state converse open. The present upper theorem is proved on that conditional-moment class after adding only \(d_e\le Cd_b\); its hard scaled-Rademacher, binary-action family is a bounded subclass, so the converse transfers upward to the full moment class. The new result is the uniform radius law joining \(C=1\), shrinking \(C_T-1\), and fixed \(C>1\). MehrabiWager2025 remains a fully observed comparator because its stationary ratio is observable or estimable. ZhangJiang2024 and TennenholtzShalitMannor2020 require belief, proxy, rank, or decoupling structure absent here. KallusUehara2020 and LiaoKlasnjaMurphy2021 provide fully observed efficiency and mobile-health endpoints. The finite insulin construction adapts the LuckettEtAl2020 and MaahsEtAl2012 setting used in HuWager2023 Section 5.2; it does not assert that the original continuous simulator satisfies this finite-state contraction and overlap class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The observed-filtration posterior recursion, stationary initial-window calculation, explicit \(T\varepsilon_C^2\alpha^{2Q}L^{-Q}\) KL modulus, conditional-moment PHIW covariance bound, uniform frontier, and interval-certified finite insulin demonstration are now proved in the note's core. The finite insulin model remains an artificial refreshed discretization, and no claim is made that the original continuous simulator in HuWager2023 or LuckettEtAl2020 satisfies finite-state uniform contraction or latent stationary overlap. The theorem is a mean-squared-error result and does not supply confidence intervals or a test of the latent-overlap assertion.
body.honest_scope: The theorem covers one stationary trajectory, arbitrary finite observed, hidden, and action alphabets with no cardinality bounds, Hu and Wager's conditional first- and second-moment reward envelope, known memoryless policies, uniform contraction, and latent joint-state stationary overlap. Its constants are uniform over \(C\ge1\) and may depend only on \(t_0,\zeta,M_1,M_2\). The hard family is binary and bounded but is used only as a subclass for the converse; the upper bound holds on the full moment class. The result does not cover a uniformly bounded hidden alphabet, nonstationary starts, unknown policies, proxy-assisted estimators, confidence intervals, policy-learning regret, or the original continuous insulin simulator. The refreshed \(360\)-state illustration demonstrates the interpretation but is not itself a minimax-hard sequence.
body.interpretation: A latent occupancy assurance has a quantitative value only through its distance from equality. Near \(d_e=d_b\), it permits shorter observable histories and reaches parametric precision once \(q_C=O(T^{-1/2})\). A fixed nonunit bound, even if substantively small, leaves the worst-case hidden-state exponent unchanged when latent cardinality is unrestricted. The refreshed discretization has rewards in \([-1,0]\), so it fits the re-anchored moment envelope, for example with \(M_1=1\) and any \(M_2>1\). In that insulin illustration, bounded latent physiological occupancy therefore does not by itself justify immediate weighting; shorter histories require an assurance that tightens with trajectory length or additional observed state or proxy information.
